title: Number Series

steps.title: Look for a repeating rule
steps.content: A number series is generated by a rule. Start by checking consecutive differences. If differences are constant, it is an arithmetic pattern. If not, check second differences, ratios, squares or alternating rules.
steps.tip: Write the differences below the series before guessing.

steps.title: Recognize multiplication patterns
steps.content: If differences grow quickly, check multiplication or division. A series may also alternate two separate patterns in odd and even positions.
steps.example: 2, 6, 18, 54… multiply by 3 each time, so next = 162.

steps.title: Alternating pattern
steps.explanation: Odd positions: 2,4,6,8. Even positions: 5,7,9. Next is 8.

steps.title: Squares and cubes
steps.content: Compare terms with nearby perfect squares or cubes. For example, 1, 8, 27, 64 are 1³, 2³, 3³, 4³.
steps.example: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 are consecutive squares. The next term is 36.

questions.explanation: Differences are 3,5,7,9; next difference is 11, so 27+11=38.

learning_objectives: Use differences to test candidate rules.
Avoid choosing a pattern that fits only two terms.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Any two terms define the intended pattern.
common_misconceptions.correction: Use several terms and prefer a simple consistent rule.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Every series is arithmetic or geometric.
common_misconceptions.correction: Some series alternate rules or use squares, cubes or changing differences.

common_misconceptions.misconception: A guessed next term is enough.
common_misconceptions.correction: Explain a rule that accounts for all given terms.

worked_examples.title: Arithmetic sequence
worked_examples.explanation: A constant first difference indicates an arithmetic sequence.

worked_examples.title: Geometric sequence
worked_examples.explanation: A constant ratio indicates a geometric sequence.

worked_examples.title: Alternating sequence
worked_examples.explanation: Separate alternating subsequences when one simple difference does not fit.

company_applications.practice: Write down differences and test the rule across all terms.
Check alternating subsequences and common powers.
Explain why the pattern fits every given term.

srs_cards.question: What are the key ideas in Number Series?
srs_cards.answer: Detect arithmetic and geometric patterns. Check alternating and interleaved sequences. Use differences to test candidate rules. Avoid choosing a pattern that fits only two terms.

srs_cards.question: Name a common mistake in Number Series.
srs_cards.answer: Use several terms and prefer a simple consistent rule.
